title: Gray-release policy and pinless entry spec for experimental open models
creator: Lena Park
description: Define a lightweight, operationally safe flow for admitting experimental community (open) models into the catalog without immediate hard pinning. Provide a gray-release (staged) policy, required compatibility annotations, telemetry gating rules and explicit acceptance criteria so runtime and Console teams can enforce fallbacks and de-risk live traffic.
problem_statement: Current intake expects either full version pinning or full rejection. This blocks rapid experimentation for community-maintained weights while creating operational risk when unpinned variants surface breaking runtime behaviour. We need a repeatable policy for 'pinless' entries that still enforces safety via staged rollout, compatibility metadata, and automated fallbacks.
goals: (1) Provide a spec that allows non-pinned/experimental models to enter the catalog behind a gray-release flag; (2) Define the metadata and compatibility annotations runtime needs to decide routing and fallbacks; (3) Specify telemetry gates and rollback criteria for promoting or demoting entries; (4) Minimize manual operator load during the first 2 weeks of traffic.
non_goals: (1) Replacing existing hard-pinning contract for enterprise-backed models; (2) Implementing the runtime routing changes — this ticket only defines the product/requirements and acceptance criteria; (3) Defining pricing/billing changes for gray-release traffic.
requirements: Catalog schema extension: allow 'pinless' boolean and 'gray_release_policy' string (values: opt-in, gradual, restricted) as top-level fields
Compatibility annotations: model must declare 'kernel_compat' (list), 'kv_cache_behavior' (enum: preserved|reset|unknown), 'max_seq_safe' (int) and 'feature_flags' (list) at intake
Runtime signals contract: define a minimal telemetry surface (latency_p50/95/99, error_rate, output_regression_score) that onboarding telemetry will emit for the first 14 days
Default soft-pin TTL: configurable per-entry, default 14 days — after TTL expires runtime can either auto-pin (if gates pass) or demote to catalog-hidden state
Staged traffic policy: initial traffic allocation steps (0%, 0.1%, 1%, 5%, 20%) with min observation window and gate checks between steps
Fallback mapping: for each unpinned variant the catalog must include at least one compatible fallback model key; runtime must support immediate failover to fallback when error thresholds hit
Console UX: an onboarding card that surfaces compatibility annotations, active gray-release allocation, recent telemetry, and a single-click rollback/pause
Evaluation checklist: incoming model must pass a lightweight sanity suite (sanity-runner) that includes tokenization parity and deterministic forward pass for a fixed prompt set
Access controls: only staff with 'model-catalog:approve-pinless' can create gray-release entries; audit log entry required for each promotion/demotion

Telemetry gating: define numeric thresholds for promotion (e.g., p95 latency within 1.5x baseline, error_rate < 0.5%, output_regression_score delta < 0.03) and for rollback (sustained violation over 10m window)
Operator alerts: integrate with PagerDuty playbooks for critical failures during gray-release windows
acceptance_criteria: Product spec reviewed and signed off by Runtime, Console, and Risk teams
Catalog schema PR merged with backward-compatible migration plan documented
Console mockups validated by Design and Developer Experience with an accessible rollback action
A test harness demonstrates staged allocation steps and runtime fallback when injected errors are triggered
Telemetry gating thresholds codified and example dashboards created in Console showing a synthetic gray-release run
RBAC controls tested: only users with the right permission can create/promote pinless entries
Onboarding checklist (sanity-runner) executes in CI and flags any tokenization mismatches
Promote/demote actions are recorded in audit logs and surfaced as events in customer-facing activity feed for the model entry
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Spec review and internal signoff (2 weeks). Phase 1: Catalog schema and Console UX landing (3 weeks). Phase 2: Runtime telemetry surface + test harness (3 weeks). Phase 3: Pilot with 3 low-risk community models on internal staging then limited public pilot (4 weeks). Each phase gated by acceptance criteria.
migration_path: Existing pinned entries are unaffected. For unpinned historical entries we will add 'pinless':false by default. Admins can opt-in entries for gray-release via the Console import flow. Migration notes and a small script to annotate prior entries will be provided.
risks: Undetected model regressions affecting many customers during early traffic windows
Ambiguous compatibility annotations leading runtime to make unsafe routing decisions
Operational overhead if telemetry gating thresholds are too conservative leading to many manual rollbacks
Security or IP concerns from admitting community weights — legal review required in edge cases
